This is bad and contributes to my view that the Pacers are maybe the most overrated organization in the league.


Ryan Glasspiegel (@sportsrapport)

Scott Agness, who has been covering the Pacers and Fever for eons, says he got his credentials revoked for doing run of the mill reporting, and provides all the receipts:



— https://nitter.net/sportsrapport/status/2061877407246585962#m

Here's our Joseph George (@jogeor_ ) with more, PLUS our NBA Finals chat with special guest @NateDuncanNBA!

natesilver.net/p/the-spurs-a…

Part II of our NBA Finals preview is up!

The Spurs are one of the youngest *playoff* teams (not just Finals teams) ever.

Empirically, playoff experience matters.

But so far, their poise is outweighing that.
The fact that it's tolerated is bad too a textbook example of learned helplessness.
Like honestly "it's going to take us several weeks to tell you who won the election" is failed state shit and should be much more stigmatized.
The fact that California elections often can't be resolved for weeks is kind of insane and not common in other electoral systems around the world.

Whether there's something more there or not (maybe not), there's a little bit of Biden post-debate in the @katz_morris strategy, i.e., let's try to gut this through until the withdrawal deadline passes in mid-July and Dems *literally* have no choice.

Yeah, it's pretty bad. Saying "this doesn't matter, Graham is focused on the issues," etc. is fine and sort of on-brand, but the threats against the former staffer are very dubious and also very establishment-y and "political" for that matter.


Brien Jackson (@Brien_Jackson)

It's worth pointing out that, contra the Platner degenerates, it is absolutely not normal campaign behavior to threaten a former staffer if they refuse to go on the record with an outright lie to major media organizations.

BTW you're also gambling on something much worse not coming out after the withdrawal deadline passes in mid-July, which I don't think anyone in this argument is so dishonest as to not be concerned about.

The whole narrative they built is Platner had youthful, drunken indiscretions and was on a redemption arc. Which was always probably bullshit, and this story speaks to that. Voters can/should vote for him anyway if they share his policy goals! But that's up for them to decide.

Look I don't really GAF who's sexting who. But why are Platner campaign advisors like @katz_morris  threatening ex-staffers as if they disclosed nuclear secrets? Because in a democracy, it's the people's job to decide what matters, and they know it might be damaging.


austerity is theft (@wideofthepost)

There is no “sexting scandal.” There’s nothing scandalous here. The Platners resolved this before they decided to run for senate and brought this up on their own campaign self-vetting — which t
